title: She Chose Retirement Over the Next Tech Overhaul. It Unlocked a Hidden Social Security Window.
excerpt: She pulled in six figures before walking away from her job at 63, which should have wiped out her Social Security checks for the rest of the year. A little-k...

Quick Read

  • A first-year grace rule lets new retirees use a monthly earnings test, so pre-retirement wages like $140,000 don't cancel benefits for the rest of the year.

  • Investment income, 401(k) withdrawals, and pensions don't count toward the earnings test, making the grace-year rule genuinely useful for professionals with savings.

  • Retiring midyear creates a low-income window ideal for Roth conversions, letting retirees deliberately fill the 12% and 22% brackets before RMDs raise their taxable income permanently.

  • Two retirees, same $1 million, same 4% rule, buy one finished with $1.4 million, the other hit $0 in 12 years. Our free reader guide explains the flaw that separated them, and the income-first method built to avoid it.

The Midyear Exit That Changed Her Math

She earned about $140,000 in a senior role through midyear. Then her employer rolled out an AI-driven restructuring, offered an early-retirement package, and she took it at 63. The Wall Street Journal has documented this pattern: older professionals choosing to step away rather than absorb one more technology overhaul, sometimes years earlier than planned.

She files for Social Security and reads the earnings test rules. For someone below full retirement age (FRA), the annual limit is a small fraction of what she has already earned, and Social Security withholds $1 for every $2 above that cap. On paper, she owes back every check she was hoping to collect this year.

A recurring question in retirement forums: I earned six figures before retiring in July, does that mean Social Security pays me nothing until January?

The First-Year Grace Rule That Rescues Her

Here is the twist most people never hear. In the first year someone retires, Social Security lets them use a monthly earnings test instead of the annual one. This grace-year rule is designed for exactly her situation: a big paycheck in the first half of the year, no wages after.

The 4% Rule is Broken, Built On A World That No Longer Exists

Every retiree knows about the 4% rule, but it frames retirement as a slow liquidation and still causes retirees with seven-figure accounts to agonize over a dinner out.

There's a different way to run the math that makes more sense today. Build an income floor — dividends, interest, and Social Security that cover your essential bills every month — and you never have to sell shares into a down market just to pay them.

Our free reader guide, The 4% Rule Is Broken, walks through it in about 15 minutes. Access the report here.

Under the monthly test, she can receive a check for any month in which her wages fall below roughly one-twelfth of the annual limit and she is considered retired. That earlier $140,000 does not disqualify her. What matters is what she earns each month after she stops working. Most months she will bring in zero from wages, which sits comfortably under the monthly threshold.

  • 第一年的宽限规则允许新退休人员使用每月收入测试，因此退休前工资（例如 140,000 美元）不会取消今年剩余时间的福利。
  • 投资收入、401(k) 提款和养老金不计入收入测试，这使得宽限年规则对有储蓄的专业人士真正有用。
  • 年中退休为罗斯转换创造了一个理想的低收入窗口，让退休人员在 RMD 永久提高应税收入之前故意填补 12% 和 22% 的区间。
  • 两名退休人员，同样的 100 万美元，同样的 4% 规则，买了一个最终以 140 万美元完成，另一个在 12 年内跌至 0 美元。 我们的免费读者指南解释了将他们分开的缺陷，以及为避免该缺陷而建立的收入优先方法。

年中退学改变了她的数学

截至年中，她担任高级职位的收入约为 14 万美元。 然后她的雇主推出了人工智能驱动的重组，并提供了提前退休方案，她在 63 岁时接受了这一方案。 《华尔街日报》记录了这种模式：年长的专业人士选择离开，而不是接受另一次技术改革，有时比计划早了几年。

她申请社会保障并阅读收入测试规则。 对于低于完全退休年龄 (FRA) 的人来说，年度限额只是她已赚取收入的一小部分，社会保障每超出该限额 2 美元，将扣留 1 美元。 从表面上看，她欠下了今年希望收到的每张支票。

退休论坛中经常出现的一个问题：我在七月退休前赚了六位数，这是否意味着社会保障在一月之前不会向我支付任何费用？

拯救她的第一年宽限规则

这是大多数人从未听过的转折。 在某人退休的第一年，社会保障允许他们使用月度收入测试而不是年度收入测试。 这个宽限年的规定正是针对她的情况而设计的：上半年工资很高，之后就没有工资了。

4% 规则被打破，建立在一个不再存在的世界上

每个退休人员都知道 4% 的规则，但它将退休视为一种缓慢的清算，并且仍然导致拥有七位数账户的退休人员为外出就餐而苦恼。

今天有一种更有意义的不同的数学计算方法。 建立一个收入底线——股息、利息和社会保障，足以支付你每月的基本账单——你永远不需要在低迷的市场上出售股票来支付这些费用。

我们的免费读者指南《4% 规则被打破》大约需要 15 分钟。 在此访问报告。

根据月度测试，只要她的工资低于年度限额的大约十二分之一，她就可以收到一张支票，并且她被视为退休。 之前的 14 万美元并没有取消她的资格。 重要的是她停止工作后每个月的收入。 大多数时候，她的工资都是零，完全低于每月的门槛。
